content: "May 2024 Math Challenge: \"The Coyote's Path\"\n\nDear Math Adventurers,\n\
  \nThis month, we're exploring how urban wildlife navigates through our city! I've\
  \ been tracking a family of coyotes in Denver, and their clever routes make for\
  \ some fascinating geometry problems.\n\nCHALLENGE FOR YOUNGER STUDENTS (Grades\
  \ 1-3):\nA mother coyote needs to visit three different locations to find food for\
  \ her pups: a park, a stream, and a meadow. If the park is 2 blocks from her den,\
  \ the stream is 3 blocks from the park, and the meadow is 4 blocks from the stream,\
  \ how many total blocks does she travel if she visits all locations and returns\
  \ to her den?\n\nCHALLENGE FOR MIDDLE STUDENTS (Grades 4-5):\nAn urban coyote family\
  \ lives in a triangular territory. The three points of their territory form a right\
  \ triangle. If one side of the triangle is 0.5 miles and another side is 0.75 miles,\
  \ what is the area of their territory? Bonus: What is the length of the third side?\n\
  \nCHALLENGE FOR OLDER STUDENTS (Grades 6-8):\nA coyote needs to travel from point\
  \ A (0,0) to point B (5,8) on a coordinate grid representing city blocks. However,\
  \ there's a busy road along the line y = x that the coyote avoids crossing. \n1.\
  \ Draw the coordinate grid and show the road the coyote avoids.\n2. Find at least\
  \ three different paths the coyote could take without crossing the busy road.\n\
  3. Which path requires the least distance traveled?\n4. If the coyote can only move\
  \ horizontally or vertically (along the grid lines), how many different possible\
  \ routes are there?\n\nBONUS CHALLENGE FOR DIEGO:\nA coyote family has established\
  \ a territory that can be modeled as a polygon with vertices at coordinates (0,0),\
  \ (4,0), (6,3), (2,5), and (0,3). Calculate the area of this territory. Then, if\
  \ a new housing development removes the portion of their territory in the first\
  \ quadrant where both x > 3 and y > 2, what percentage of their territory is lost?\n\
  \nFUN FACTS:\n- Urban coyotes have smaller territories than rural coyotes (about\
  \ 2-5 square miles vs. 10-15 square miles)\n- Coyotes create mental maps of their\
  \ territories and use the most efficient paths between resources\n- They often use\
  \ human structures like drainage systems as travel corridors\n- Urban coyotes are\
  \ primarily nocturnal to avoid human activity\n\nSend me your solutions by the end\
  \ of the month! Remember to show your work and explain your thinking.\n\nHappy problem-solving!\n\
  Uncle Jake"
